monk_attribute_cost_contract.attribute_contract: For every trait whose numeric final value Monk actively modifies, full investment yields 80-90% of the comparable optimized fully equipped TMM specialist's final numerical attribute. Report actual nonlinear performance as a secondary check.
monk_attribute_cost_contract.comparison_requires: Matched metric, specialist loadout, attribute IDs and cap/stack rules. Monk unarmored legal equipment. Non-numeric abilities tracked separately. Explicit zero/signed/reduction semantics.
monk_attribute_cost_contract.tyz_cost_contract: Total spendable Tyz SP for ALL purchasable Monk tree ranks ~= 10x the canonical completed non-Monk specialist tree (9-11x provisional band). Baseline/native discipline points are NOT Tyz SP.
monk_attribute_cost_contract.xp_contract: Owner selected 1.02 default; configurable 1.00–1.20 NeoForge server config in PR #161. Core prototype branch still hardcodes 1.2 until PR merged. 1.01 is alternate. With g>1 Monk ~10x points yields >10x ordinary XP in matched fresh-start model; fixed boss/ritual rewards affect real play.
monk_attribute_cost_contract.nominal_ordinary_xp_formula: XP_base_for_N_lifetime_levels=1000*(pow(1.2,N)-1)/(1.2-1) from P=0, no fixed award; 10*N ratio is far greater than 10 for nontrivial N.

ars_thread_modifier_collision_audit.issue: Ars in-game documentation explicitly states same-type threads apply once per armor set, not cumulatively. Source PerkUtil.countForPerk selects maximum slot rank for relevant per-perk calculations. For attribute threads, duplicate IDs mean additional copies must NOT be counted; slot selection with duplicates need not be assumed because optimal legal loadout uses exactly one level-six Capacity thread and one separate level-six Spell Power thread.
ars_thread_modifier_collision_audit.compared_enchantment_behavior: Minecraft enchantment attribute effects postfix the modifier id with the armor slot name, so identical Mana Boost/Mana Regen enchantments on different armor slots are designed to coexist.
ars_thread_modifier_collision_audit.runtime_gate: Verify exact ATM10 Unobtainium level-six perk-slot availability and effective final attributes. No duplicate-thread stacking is assumed.

monk_mxp_growth_scenario_comparison.ordinary_xp_model: one SP per 1000 effective XP; routine awards effective=base/(growth^P), P lifetime MXP levels. From lifetime P=0: nominal_base_xp_to_N_points=1000*((growth^N)-1)/(growth-1); growth=1 gives 1000*N.
monk_mxp_growth_scenario_comparison.earlier_xp_goal_update: At growth=1, Monk 10x points => 10x ordinary XP, not significantly-more-than-10x. At growth>1, ratio can be vastly higher; this is an open design tradeoff, not a locked runtime rule.

Do not claim 1.1 remains user preferred; it is a high-growth regression comparison.
